Area.evidence_source: It is interesting how much the participants discussed the stereotypic male image and its negative impact on them. It seems that 'the masculinity image' had the effect that they felt that they were not allowed to show their emotions and had difficulty disclosing trauma. The masculinity image can therefore be a certain silencing of the emotional life of men since they experienced feeling unable to express their feelings and being unable to express themselves about difficult things. Some participants blamed upbringing while others blamed society, that 'society' had created this norm around manhood and how men should behave and express themselves or not behave and express themselves. This concurs with ideas about how restricted emotions (19) and masculine qualities and roles are considered typical of, appropriate for, and expected of boys and men (18) and are good examples of the negative impacts of hegemonic masculinity on men's health-related behaviour (22). Parents probably play a big part and maybe it is often thoughtlessness to raise boys so that they do not cry but nowadays we should know better. If suppressing emotion is a learned behaviour, then we must be able to reverse this.
